inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $30.5M (total SBC expense; the cash-flow add-back ShareBasedCompensation is $27.3M, the difference being cash-settled awards) plus an estimated $6.0M of cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement (last tagged FY2022 $5.2M, H1-2023 $4.6M; no combined figure published). Interest income not stripped: IDEX is net debt (net interest expense $64.4M FY2025).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $247.8M; H1-2026 $153.4M. Buybacks exceed SBC ~7x, so the flat share count is funded, not a convention. Dividends $212.6M FY2025 ($2.92/yr run-rate) are value-neutral distributions outside the model.
inputs.share_count_basis: Cover-page shares 73.72M at 2026-07-24 (Q2-2026 10-Q) plus 0.2M dilutive securities (Q2-2026 diluted 74.2M less basic 74.0M) = 73.9M fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet 2026-06-30: long-term debt $1,858.5M + current $0.4M (+$8.4M other borrowings per DB total_debt 1,867.3) less cash $621.3M. Dec-2025 net debt was $1,250.5M; H1-2026 FCF ($263M) was fully returned via buybacks + dividends ($260M), so pairing a June balance sheet with a full-FY2026 year-1 flow does not double count. Operating lease liability ($121.9M at Dec-2025) NOT added to net debt (see lease_treatment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST, Sept 2026), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 -> cost of equity ~9.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (3.0-6.0% senior notes), 23% tax -> 3.5% after tax; debt ~10% of EV ($1.9B debt vs ~$17B market cap) -> WACC ~8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not by per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): US GAAP operating-lease cost ($36.6M FY2025) sits inside operating expenses, so it is already deducted from EBITDA/EBIT in the flows. Lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is inside the EBITDA margin, not a second line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is -$1.4M at 2026-06-30 (immaterial); no NCI deduction and no attributable adjustment.
inputs.da_note: FY2025 D&A $206.5M = depreciation $75.8M (2.2% of revenue) + amortization of acquired intangibles $130.7M (3.8%). Capex is only 1.8-2.2% of revenue because most D&A is book amortization from ~$1.5B of acquisitions since 2023 (Mott $985M in 2024). da_pct_path tapers 5.9% -> 4.5% as the acquired-intangible schedule runs off with no new M&A cash in the model; the taper raises taxable EBIT, which is the conservative direction.
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer: receivables + inventory exceed payables (NWC ~17-20% of sales), so growth consumes cash. wc_capture_pct is negative (-15% of the revenue increase); FY2023-25 OCF ran $37-53M below NI + D&A + SBC in growth years.
inputs.tax_note: Cash taxes paid FY2025 $134.6M on pretax $632.6M = 21.3%; GAAP provision 23.7%. On an unlevered EBIT base (adding back the ~$15M tax shield on net interest) the cash rate is ~21-22%. Path starts at 22% and drifts to 23% (statutory 21% federal + state + foreign mix; management guides ~22-23%).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, US industrial, moderately cyclical). Not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco; no dual currency; SBC is non-zero so house/street band is real but narrow (~1% of revenue). Fresh build, first valuation of this ticker. FY0 = FY2025 (last complete fiscal year, Dec year-end); Y1 = FY2026, the guidance year (organic +5-6%, adj EPS $8.70-8.85 raised Aug-2026; H1-2026 revenue +7.6% reported; Q2 orders +29% organic on HST data-center liquid cooling and semicap). Year-1 is discounted a full period although three quarters of FY2026 have elapsed, which is the folder convention and mildly conservative. FY2025 EBITDA (pre-SBC, adjusted basis) = operating income 699.3 + D&A 206.5 + SBC 30.5 = 936.3 = 27.1% of revenue; H1-2026 ~27.7%. Terminal cap 18x owner FCF: a quality compounder but a diversified industrial, so below the 20x default and above the 12-15x pure-cyclical band. Price is the 2026-09-28 regular close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-path 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2026 guidance +7% decelerating to 3%), cross-checked against the FY2015-25 revenue CAGR of 5.5% which includes ~$2.5B of acquisitions the model does not fund
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (9.7-9.8%) exceeds 3yr revenue CAGR (2.8%) and 3yr EPS CAGR (-6.1%) by far more than 30%. Equity growth is retained earnings accumulating on a goodwill-heavy acquisitive balance sheet ($1B Mott deal 2024), not operating growth; EPS fell FY2022-25 on Mott amortization, higher interest and the 2024 industrial destocking. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC expense less equity-award taxes; no interest strip). Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 3.4% vs reported 3.6%: SBC is growing marginally faster than FCF but is ~1% of revenue so the gap is immaterial. FY2020 (COVID) is the 5yr base and flatters revenue growth; FY2022 (post-COVID peak EPS $7.74) is the 3yr base and depresses EPS growth. Windows: FY2022->FY2025 (3yr), FY2020->FY2025 (5yr), FY2015->FY2025 (10yr). Owner FCF: FY2020 490.6, FY2022 459.6, FY2025 580.3.

base.narrative: FY2026 at the top of guidance plus FX (+7%), FY2027 carried by the record backlog (+6.5%), then a glide to 3% as the data-center/semicap order surge normalises into IDEX's long-run 3-5% organic rate. Adjusted EBITDA margin expands ~140bp over the decade on 8020 mix and HST growth, to 29%. No acquisition cash is modelled, so acquired-intangible amortization runs off (D&A 5.9% -> 4.5% of revenue) while capex holds at 2.2%.

bull.narrative: AI data-center liquid cooling, performance pneumatics and semicap ultra-pure fluidics prove to be a multi-year secular wave rather than a capex spike: HST compounds high-single/low-double digits through FY2028, FMT water/chemical and space & defense add to it, and 8020 lifts adjusted EBITDA margin to 30.5%. Ten-year revenue CAGR ~5.9%, terminal growth 3%.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance; the hyperscaler capex cycle rolls over in 2027 and HST orders reverse the way industrial demand did in the 2024 destocking, producing a -3% year in FY2028. Low-cost Asian pump/valve competition compresses FMT pricing, adjusted EBITDA margin troughs at 25.5% and only recovers to 27%. Growth settles at 2.5% with terminal 2%. No solvency or covenant risk (net debt/EBITDA ~1.3x), so this is an earnings bear, not a survival bear.

scenario_narratives.base: IDEX's axes are (1) whether the FY2026 HST order surge -- Q2 orders +29% organic, driven by data-center liquid cooling and semiconductor capital equipment -- converts into two years of above-trend revenue before normalising, (2) how much of the 8020 margin programme reaches adjusted EBITDA, and (3) how the legacy FMT/FSDP segments grow against low-cost Asian competition. Base: FY2026 +7% (top of the raised 5-6% organic guide plus FX), FY2027 +6.5% on record backlog, decelerating to 3% by FY2033; adjusted EBITDA margin 27.6% -> 29%; capex 2.2%, working capital absorbs 15% of each year's revenue increase; cash tax 22% -> 23%; WACC 8.5%, terminal 2.5%, 18x cap. No M&A cash and hence no acquired-revenue growth: the ~$2.5B spent on deals since 2023 is why the trailing 10-year revenue CAGR (5.5%) exceeds the organic run-rate.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-infrastructure demand for precision fluidics and pneumatics is a durable multi-year buildout, semicap recovers on top of it, and space & defense keeps growing. HST compounds at high-single/low-double digits through FY2028 and the group reaches a 30.5% adjusted EBITDA margin. Terminal growth 3%. This case needs several independent things to go right at once -- hyperscaler capex persistence, a semicap upcycle and continued 8020 margin capture -- which is why it is not weighted above the bear.
scenario_narratives.bear: The growth acceleration is concentrated in AI-linked end markets that prove to be a capex spike, not a secular wave. Hyperscaler spending slows in 2027, HST orders reverse, and the group repeats the 2024 destocking pattern with a -3% revenue year in FY2028. FMT pricing erodes under Chinese/Indian competition and the adjusted EBITDA margin troughs at 25.5%, recovering only to 27%. Balance sheet remains sound throughout (no refinancing risk; $800M revolver extended Sept-2026), so the bear is an earnings-and-multiple outcome, not a distress outcome.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear weight up because the FY2026-27 acceleration is concentrated in hyperscaler/semicap capex -- the Analysis JSON flags the AI-capex cycle as a moderate risk and IDEX has had two order downturns in the last decade (2015-16 oil/industrial, 2024 destocking) -- while the balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA ~1.3x) keeps this from going higher. Bull weight down because the bull case requires three independent things to persist at once (data-center liquid cooling demand, a semicap upcycle, and continued margin capture) and the stock already sits near its 52-week high at ~32x trailing earnings.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IDEX is a high-quality, niche-leading fluidics compounder with ~45% gross margins, ~27% adjusted EBITDA margins, low capex intensity and a funded flat share count. The valuation question is not whether the business is good but what a buyer at today's price is paying for: the house DCF capitalises FY2035 owner FCF at 18x / 8.5% WACC, and even the bull case assumes the AI-capex-led HST surge fades to a mid-single-digit compounder by the early 2030s. The historical record supports that: 10-year revenue CAGR of 5.5% including ~$2.5B of acquisitions, owner-FCF 5-year CAGR of 3.4%. Because M&A cash is not modelled, the model also gives no credit for future deals; the reader should treat acquired growth as an upside the company must pay for.
key_risks_to_valuation: Data-center/semicap order surge (HST +47% organic orders in Q2-2026) proves to be a capex spike rather than a multi-year wave -- the bear path
Low-cost Asian competition in commodity pumps and valves compresses FMT pricing and margin
Acquisition integration and goodwill impairment risk on the $1B Mott deal and future bolt-ons; no M&A cash in the model means acquired growth is neither counted nor charged
Global industrial capex / PMI sensitivity; 2024 showed a flat-revenue year is possible with no macro recession
Terminal value is the majority of enterprise value at an 8.5% WACC; a 1pp WACC move shifts base IV materially (see sensitivity grid)
Tariff and trade-policy exposure across a global manufacturing footprint
